1.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
1.solution:
For a vehicle on a curved road the normal reaction depends on the centripetal requirement.
Horizontal: \(N = mg\).
Convex (centre below): \(mg - N = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow N = mg - \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} < mg\).
Concave (centre above): \(N - mg = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}\Rightarrow N = mg + \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} > mg\).
Hence the normal reaction is maximum on the concave road.

2.solution:
Each alpha emission reduces mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2; each beta emission increases atomic number by 1 (mass number unchanged).
Mass: \(226 - 206 = 20 = 4\times(\text{no. of }\alpha)\Rightarrow\) number of \(\alpha = 5\).
Atomic number after 5 \(\alpha\): \(88 - 10 = 78\). To reach 82: \(82 - 78 = 4\) beta particles.
So 5 alpha and 4 beta.

3.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
3.solution:
Distance between 1st and 10th maxima \(= 9\omega = (16.75 - 14.50) = 2.25\) mm, so fringe width \(\omega = 0.25\) mm.
New fringe width \(\omega' = \dfrac{5500}{6000}\times0.25 = 0.229\) mm (\(\omega\propto\lambda\)).
The central (zero order) maximum position is unchanged: \(y_{0} = y_{1} - \omega = 14.50 - 0.25 = 14.25\) mm.
Tenth order: \(y_{10} = y_{0} + 10\omega' = 14.25 + 10\times0.229 = 16.54\approx16.55\) mm.

4.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
4.solution:
Phosphorus is a donor, making the silicon n-type with \(n_{e}\approx10^{21}/m^{3}\). Mass-action law: \(n_{e}n_{h} = n_{i}^{2}\).
\[n_{h} = \frac{n_{i}^{2}}{n_{e}} = \frac{(10^{16})^{2}}{10^{21}} = \frac{10^{32}}{10^{21}} = 10^{11}/m^{3}.\]

5.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
5.solution:
For a conical/banking situation the bob hangs at angle \(\theta\) with \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^{2}}{rg}\).
\[\tan\theta = \frac{(10)^{2}}{20\times10} = \frac{100}{200} = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.5).\]

6.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
6.solution:
Limit of resolution of the eye (treating the pupil as an aperture) gives angular resolution \(\Delta\theta = \dfrac{1.22\lambda}{D}\) where \(D = 2\times0.25 = 0.5\) cm is the pupil diameter. Minimum separation at distance \(L = 25\) cm:
\[\Delta x = L\,\Delta\theta = \frac{1.22\lambda L}{D} = \frac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}\times0.25}{0.5\times10^{-2}} \approx 3\times10^{-5}\ \text{m} = 30\ \mu\text{m}.\]

7.solution:
By Gauss's law the net flux depends only on the net enclosed charge: \(\phi = \dfrac{q_{net}}{\varepsilon_{0}}\).
Net charge \(= 2 - 3 + 4 - 4 - 1 = -2\ \mu\text{C}\), so the flux is \(\dfrac{-2\,\mu\text{C}}{\varepsilon_{0}}\), and among the printed options the keyed one corresponds to a net charge of \(-2\,\mu\text{C}\).
7.note: Stem lists charges as 2, -3, 4, -4, -1 microC giving net -2 microC. The option set is garbled (mixes flux q/epsilon0 forms with a bare charge '-2 microC'); the keyed option B encodes the correct net charge -2 microC, so kept as printed.

8.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
8.solution:
Sphere about diameter: \(I_{s} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^{2}\); cylinder about axis: \(I_{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^{2}\). Given \(\omega_{c} = 2\omega_{s}\).
\[\frac{E_{s}}{E_{c}} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}I_{s}\omega_{s}^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}I_{c}\omega_{c}^{2}} = \frac{\frac{2}{5}mR^{2}\,\omega_{s}^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}mR^{2}\,(2\omega_{s})^{2}} = \frac{\frac{2}{5}}{\frac{1}{2}\times4} = \frac{2/5}{2} = \frac{1}{5}.\]

9.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
9.solution:
First echo: distance to nearer cliff \(= \dfrac{vt_{1}}{2} = \dfrac{340\times1}{2} = 170\) m.
Second echo: distance to farther cliff \(= \dfrac{vt_{2}}{2} = \dfrac{340\times3}{2} = 510\) m.
Distance between cliffs \(= 170 + 510 = 680\) m.

10.solution:
Series of 10 capacitors \(C_{1}\): \(C_{s} = \dfrac{C_{1}}{10}\), charged to 4V, energy \(E_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_{1}}{10}(4V)^{2}\).
Parallel of 8 capacitors \(C_{2}\): \(C_{p} = 8C_{2}\), charged to V, energy \(E_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(8C_{2})V^{2}\).
Setting \(E_{1}=E_{2}\): \(\dfrac{C_{1}}{10}\times16 = 8C_{2}\Rightarrow C_{2} = \dfrac{16C_{1}}{80} = \dfrac{C_{1}}{5}.\)

11.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
11.solution:
Same mass and same material; solid sphere is more compact (smaller radius) but the standard comparison at equal mass and radius gives \(I_{s} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^{2}\) and \(I_{h} = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^{2}\).
\[\frac{I_{s}}{I_{h}} = \frac{2/5}{2/3} = \frac{3}{5} < 1 \Rightarrow I_{h} > I_{s}.\]
The hollow sphere has mass distributed farther from the axis, so \(I_{h} > I_{s}\).

12.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
12.solution: Induced charge \(q = \displaystyle\int i\,dt = \int\frac{1}{R}\frac{d\phi}{dt}dt = \frac{\Delta\phi}{R}\). It depends on the total change in magnetic flux (and resistance), not on the rate of change.

13.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
13.solution:
A liquid film has two surfaces, so work done \(= T\times2\Delta A\).
\(A_{1} = 5\times4 = 20\ \text{cm}^{2}\), \(A_{2} = 7\times8 = 56\ \text{cm}^{2}\), \(\Delta A = 36\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^{2}\).
\[T = \frac{W}{2\Delta A} = \frac{3\times10^{-4}}{2\times36\times10^{-4}} = \frac{3}{72} \approx 0.04\ \text{N/m}.\]

14.solution:
Kelvin reading \(x\) means Celsius \(= x - 273\). Fahrenheit \(= \dfrac{9}{5}(x-273) + 32\). Set equal to \(x\):
\[x = \frac{9}{5}(x-273) + 32 \Rightarrow x - 32 = \frac{9}{5}(x-273) \Rightarrow 5x - 160 = 9x - 2457 \Rightarrow 4x = 2297 \Rightarrow x = 574.25 \approx 574.\]
14.note: Filed under Thermal Properties (temperature-scale conversion); no dedicated scale subtopic exists, closest thermal subtopic used.

15.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
15.solution:
Capillary rise \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g} \propto \dfrac{1}{g}\). With \(g_{m} = \dfrac{g_{e}}{6}\):
\[\frac{h_{m}}{h_{e}} = \frac{g_{e}}{g_{m}} = 6 \Rightarrow h_{m} = 6h_{e}.\]
The rise on the moon is six times that on the earth.

16.subtopic: Lenses — Lens Formula, Power, and Lensmaker
16.solution: For two thin lenses in contact \(P = P_{1} + P_{2} = \dfrac{1}{f_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{f_{2}}\). With the simplified relation \(f\propto R\) used here, taking each focal length proportional to its radius, the combined power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{f_{2}} \propto \dfrac{1}{R_{1}}+\dfrac{1}{R_{2}} = \dfrac{R_{1}+R_{2}}{R_{1}R_{2}}\).

17.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
17.solution: By kinetic theory the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is \(\dfrac{3}{2}kT\), which depends only on temperature. At a given temperature this average kinetic energy is the same for all molecules (velocity and momentum differ because masses differ).

18.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
18.solution: In a common-emitter amplifier the output (collector) voltage is \(180^\circ\) out of phase with the input (base) voltage, i.e. a phase difference of \(\pi\) radians.

19.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
19.solution:
Restoring (spring) force provides the centripetal force on the mass at radius \((L+x)\): \(kx = m(L+x)\omega^{2}\).
With \(k = 8\ \text{N/m}\), \(m = 0.1\) kg, \(\omega = 8\) rad/s:
\[8x = 0.1\times64\times(L+x) = 6.4(L+x) \Rightarrow 8x - 6.4x = 6.4L \Rightarrow 1.6x = 6.4L \Rightarrow \frac{x}{L} = 4:1.\]
19.note: Stem dropped the spring constant value ('spring constant N/m'); from the AK working it is 8 N/m.

If the body moves in a circular path on smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed \(8rad/s\) then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be

20.solution:
Full-scale current of the voltmeter: \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{10}{50} = 0.2\) A.
To extend the range to 15 V a series resistance \(R'\) is required: \(R + R' = \dfrac{V'}{I}\Rightarrow 50 + R' = \dfrac{15}{0.2} = 75\Rightarrow R' = 25\ \Omega\) in series.

21.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
21.solution:
Incident heat splits into absorbed + reflected + transmitted: \(Q = Q_{a} + Q_{r} + Q_{t}\).
Absorbed \(= 0.6\times120 = 72\) J, transmitted \(= 12\) J.
\[Q_{r} = 120 - 72 - 12 = 36\ \text{J}.\]

22.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
22.solution:
Field at centre of a coil of \(n\) turns: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}nI}{2r}\Rightarrow n = \dfrac{2Br}{\mu_{0}I}\).
\[n = \frac{2\times3.14\times10^{-4}\times8\times10^{-2}}{12.56\times10^{-7}\times0.4} = \frac{5.024\times10^{-5}}{5.024\times10^{-7}} = 100.\]
22.note: Stem dropped the leading digit of the field; from the AK working B = 3.14 x 10^-4 T.
22.stemOverride: A circular coil of wire consisting of ' \(n\) ' turns each of radius 8 cm carries a current of 0.4 A . The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of coil is \(3.14 \times10^{- 4}\text{ }T\). The value of ' n ' is [Take \(\mu_{0}= 12.56 \times10^{- 7}\) SI unit]

23.solution:
Efflux speeds: \(v_{1} = \sqrt{2g(h+x)}\) (lower hole, depth \(h+x\)) and \(v_{2} = \sqrt{2gx}\) (upper hole, depth \(x\)). Thrust from each jet \(= \rho A v^{2}\), so net horizontal force:
\[F = \rho A(v_{1}^{2} - v_{2}^{2}) = \rho A[2g(h+x) - 2gx] = 2\rho A g h \propto h.\]

24.solution: From the graph the lines give \(V = Q/C\), so the line with smaller slope has larger capacitance. For the same charge \(Q\), \(V_{A} < V_{B}\) (line A lies below line B). Hence \(C_{A} = Q/V_{A} > Q/V_{B} = C_{B}\): capacitor A has the higher capacitance.

26.subtopic: Magnetisation, Susceptibility, Permeability, and B-H-M Relations
26.solution: A paramagnetic substance has a small positive susceptibility (\(0 < \chi \ll 1\)). So it is positive and small.

27.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
27.solution:
At constant pressure the fraction of heat used as external work is \(\dfrac{\Delta W}{\Delta Q} = \dfrac{R}{C_{p}} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}\).
With \(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\): \(1 - \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4 = 40\%\).

28.solution: When the galvanometer current is zero, no current flows through the 6 V branch, so R carries the full loop current driven by the 10 V cell through the \(4\,\Omega\) resistor, and the potential drop across R must balance the 6 V cell: \(V_{R} = 6\) V. Current through the \(4\,\Omega\): \(i = \dfrac{10 - 6}{4} = 1\) A. This same current passes through R, so \(R = \dfrac{V_{R}}{i} = \dfrac{6}{1} = 6\,\Omega\).

29.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
29.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
29.solution:
Einstein's equation \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \phi + eV\):
\[\frac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = \phi + eV_{1}\ \ (i),\qquad \frac{hc}{3\lambda_{1}} = \phi + \frac{eV_{1}}{6}\ \ (ii).\]
Multiply (ii) by 6: \(\dfrac{2hc}{\lambda_{1}} = 6\phi + eV_{1}\) (iii). Subtract (i) from (iii): \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = 5\phi\). Since \(\phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{0}}\), \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{5hc}{\lambda_{0}}\Rightarrow \lambda_{0} = 5\lambda_{1}.\)

30.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats

31.solution: Three equal capacitors in series: \(\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{3}{C}\Rightarrow C_{eq} = \dfrac{C}{3}\). In series the same charge gives equal voltage across each, so the combination withstands \(V + V + V = 3V\) before breakdown. Hence \(\dfrac{C}{3},\ 3V\).

32.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
32.solution:
Power factor \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow \phi = 30^\circ\). For an L-R series circuit \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{\omega L}{R}\):
\[L = \frac{R\tan30^\circ}{\omega} = \frac{50\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{2\pi\times50} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}\,\pi}\ \text{H}\quad(f = 50\ \text{Hz}).\]

33.subtopic: Variation of g with Depth, Altitude, Density, and Latitude

34.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
34.solution:
The two straight radial portions through O contribute zero field. Each semicircle gives \(B = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{4R}\) at the centre. The currents in the two semicircles circulate oppositely, so the net field is the difference:
\[B_{net} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R_{2}} - \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R_{1}} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4}\left[\frac{1}{R_{2}} - \frac{1}{R_{1}}\right].\]

35.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
35.solution:
\(\overrightarrow{F} = (t\widehat{i} + 2t^{2}\widehat{j})\), \(m = 1\) kg, so \(\overrightarrow{a} = \overrightarrow{F}\). Velocity from rest: \(\overrightarrow{v} = \int\overrightarrow{a}\,dt = \dfrac{t^{2}}{2}\widehat{i} + \dfrac{2t^{3}}{3}\widehat{j}\).
Power \(P = \overrightarrow{F}\cdot\overrightarrow{v} = t\cdot\dfrac{t^{2}}{2} + 2t^{2}\cdot\dfrac{2t^{3}}{3} = \dfrac{t^{3}}{2} + \dfrac{4t^{5}}{3}\).
At \(t = 3\): \(P = \dfrac{27}{2} + \dfrac{4\times243}{3} = 13.5 + 324 = 337.5\) W.

36.solution:
\(g = \dfrac{4\pi^{2}l}{T^{2}}\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta g}{g} = \dfrac{\Delta l}{l} + 2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}\).
\(\dfrac{\Delta l}{l} = \dfrac{1\,\text{mm}}{1000\,\text{mm}} = 0.1\%\). Total time of 100 oscillations \(= 200\) s, least count 0.1 s, so \(\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = \dfrac{0.1}{200} = 0.05\%\).
\[\frac{\Delta g}{g} = 0.1\% + 2\times0.05\% = 0.2\%.\]

37.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
37.solution: In a centre-tap full-wave rectifier the secondary is divided by the centre tap; each diode handles half the secondary voltage, so the output with respect to each diode is \(\dfrac{1}{2}V_{s}\).
37.note: Option C text is garbled ('V_n') in extraction; it denotes (1/2)V_s, the keyed and correct value.

39.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
39.solution: Open-pipe fundamental is 80 Hz, so \(\dfrac{v}{2L} = 80\Rightarrow \dfrac{v}{L} = 160\). Closing one end gives fundamental \(\dfrac{v}{4L} = 40\) Hz, and a closed pipe produces only odd harmonics: \(40, 120, 200, 280, \dots\)

40.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
40.solution:
Maximum current at resonance: \(X_{L} = X_{C}\Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi^{2}f^{2}L}\).
\[C = \frac{1}{4\times10\times(50)^{2}\times2.5} = \frac{1}{4\times10\times2500\times2.5} = 4\times10^{-6}\ \text{F} = 4\ \mu\text{F}.\]
At resonance \(I_{max} = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{230}{11.5} = 20\) A.

41.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
41.solution: Zero specific heat means no heat exchange \(\Rightarrow\) adiabatic process, for which \(PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}\). Comparing with \(PV^{n} = \text{constant}\) gives \(n = \gamma\).

42.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
42.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
42.solution: Saturation current is proportional to the number of photoelectrons emitted per second, which increases with the intensity of incident light. (Maximum KE depends on frequency, not intensity; the effect needs the particle/photon theory; stopping potential depends on frequency and work function.) Correct statement: saturation current increases with intensity.

43.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
43.solution:
\(y = 60\sin(1200t - 6x)\) micron: amplitude \(a = 60\,\mu\text{m}\), \(\omega = 1200\), \(k = 6\).
Max particle velocity \(v_{p} = a\omega = 60\times10^{-6}\times1200 = 0.072\) m/s.
Wave velocity \(v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{1200}{6} = 200\) m/s.
\[\frac{v_{p}}{v} = \frac{0.072}{200} = 3.6\times10^{-4}.\]

44.subtopic: Satellites, Orbital Motion, and Kepler's Laws

45.subtopic: SHM Energy — Kinetic, Potential, and Total
45.solution:
T.E. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^{2}A^{2}\); K.E. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^{2}(A^{2}-x^{2})\). Given T.E. \(= n\times\)K.E. at \(x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}A\):
\[A^{2} = n(A^{2}-x^{2}) = nA^{2}\left(1 - \frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{n}{4}A^{2} \Rightarrow n = 4.\]

46.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
46.solution: By Lenz's law the induced current in the ring opposes the change in flux, exerting a force on the falling magnet that opposes its motion (upward). The net downward force is reduced, so the acceleration is less than \(g\).

47.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
47.solution: In single-slit diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima and far brighter, so the fringes have unequal width and unequal intensity. The incorrect statement is that the fringes have equal width and equal intensity.

48.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
48.solution: A p-n junction diode conducts only during the half cycles that forward-bias it (half-wave rectification), so across the load a pulsating (unidirectional, not constant) voltage appears.

49.solution: Two oppositely travelling waves of speed \(v = 12\) m/s and frequency \(n\) form a stationary wave with \(\lambda = \dfrac{v}{n} = \dfrac{12}{n}\). Distance between consecutive nodes \(= \dfrac{\lambda}{2} = \dfrac{6}{n}\).

50.subtopic: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws — Induced EMF, Current, and Charge
50.solution:
Induced emf \(|e| = \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(50t^{2} + 4) = 100t\). At \(t = 2\) s, \(|e| = 200\) V.
Current \(I = \dfrac{e}{R} = \dfrac{200}{400} = 0.5\) A.
